newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Islamist-led govt to hold key meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Islamist-led govt to hold key meeting.

text.p: Turkey's embattled Islamist-led coalition was set to hold its first cabinet meeting in eight weeks on Tuesday as a row with the secularist establishment appeared to erode its hold on power.
A deepening rift between Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists and the conservative, pro-Western wing of the coalition has forced the cancellation of a string of weekly meetings.

The coalition partners are deadlocked over an army-backed plan to restrict Koranic education for young pupils as part of a secularist campaign to erode support for Erbakan and his Islam-based Welfare Party.
"The cabinet meeting is taking place at 1700 (1400 GMT)," Erbakan's press advisor Fikret Ozkan told Reuters.
Ozkan said an earlier report, at first confirmed by his office, that the meeting had been cancelled was erroneous. "The confusion was caused by a misunderstanding," he said.
A scheduled ministers' meeting was postponed last week amid reports Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller had demanded Erbakan hand over power to her immediately to prevent the government collapsing.

Army demands that Erbakan curb an alleged religious revival since he came to power last June has exposed serious cracks in the coalition government and thrown Ciller, once the darling of the secularist establishment, on the defensive.
Newspapers said on Tuesday Erbakan had backed an army plan to sack scores of Islamist soldiers after months of military pressure.
The Milliyet daily said Erbakan signed documents approving the dishonourable discharge of 161 officers and non-commissioned officers at a meeting of the Supreme Military Council on Monday.
"Ninety percent of the expulsions were for fundamentalism and the rest for extreme leftist activities," the paper said.
Other papers carried similar reports from a six-hour closed-door meeting of the Supreme Military Council, grouping the secularist top generals and the prime minister.
Four anti-Islamist MPs from Ciller's True Path Party have resigned in recent days, reducing the government's majority on paper to one. However, vacant seats give it a larger margin.
Milliyet said the generals overruled an attempt by Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, to postpone a decision on the expulsions until August.

The top brass also warned that the small Islamist press was attacking secularists and setting them up as targets for Islamist violence, the paper said. "They gave Erbakan a caution about these publications," it said.

The generals have demanded restrictions on the growing Islamist media as part of a planned return to the strict secularism of the 1920s when republican Turkey was forged out of the ashes of the Ottoman Empire.
Erbakan has so far stalled on army anti-Islamist directives, including plans to cut religious education and enforce bans on Islamic dress.
